review_note: Every record below is backed by at least one local product photo I opened, or - for the two Expedition Handlebar Packs, whose only local assets are SVG dimension diagrams with the numerals converted to outlines - by that diagram rendered in headless Chrome and read directly. Four maker pages were fetched to confirm dimension text and closure descriptions.
render_note: A `render` block is present on every roll-top, drawcord and stretch-panel product (33 of 70) and omitted on the frame packs, top tube packs and Aero modules, whose envelopes are genuinely fixed. Brand-wide caveat for whoever draws these: on almost every Apidura rolltop the roll runs along the LENGTH (seat packs, downtube packs, tool pack, aerobar pack) or the WIDTH (handlebar packs), NOT the height. Apidura therefore publishes a height that is already the packed height, so render.hgt_cm equals dims_cm.hgt on most of these records. The axis a rolled-down render should actually shorten, and the maker MIN figure to shorten it to, is named in each `basis` string, because the render block has no field for a non-height roll axis. The Cargo Cage Packs are the only Apidura family whose roll runs along the height. See also the flag in the two Front Rack Pack render blocks, where the rule-mandated minimum and the photographed height disagree badly.

products.name: Saddle Pack
products.dims_raw: MIN 36 cm / MAX 42 cm length; 16 cm height; Tapered Width: 15 - 5 cm (5.9 - 1.9 in); 13 cm diagonal
products.dims_note: len is the MAX (unfurled) length per the dimension rule; the MIN figure is the fully rolled-down state. Height is a single published figure, not a range, so it is used as-is. wid is the wide end of the 15 -> 5 cm taper, which is the ROLLED TAIL, not the saddle end; the taper itself is carried in geometry.taper. Maker page confirms "Tapered Width: 15 - 5 cm" and a design that "narrows from front to rear".

geometry.notes: Hard-edged wedge, NARROW at the seatpost and full at the tail. dimensions-1.png measures 5 cm across the seatpost plate against 15 cm across the body and 16 cm deep at the blunt rolled tail, and the dashed outline that extends the MIN 36 / MAX 42 cm length sits at the WIDE end, so the wide end is the roll. on-bike-2.jpg confirms it: the shallow plated end clamps the post and the pack swells rearward to a big blunt roll behind the saddle. (This note previously said the opposite - deepest and widest at the nose, blading to a narrow tail - and the taper was recorded nose 1 / tail 0.33 to match. Both were wrong; tools/apply-models.mjs already carried a warning about this record.) A separate flat Hypalon tongue drops below the body at the nose to spread load onto the seatpost - render it as a thin plate, not as bag volume, and put the logo on it.

closure.hardware: Hypalon compression cradle pulling the rolled tail forward into a side-release buckle on the body

details.reflective: yellow EXPEDITION tag plus reflective accents at the buckles
details.lightMount: integrated 3-prong rear light mount at the tail end of the stiffened panel
details.fabric: laminated waterproof ripstop, matte charcoal-black, RF-welded seams, Hypalon reinforcement patches, yellow EXPEDITION tag and yellow accent stitching

mount.notes: On-bike photos show TWO wide bands crossing the seatpost (the stability strap plus the lower run of the compression cradle) even though the page lists one stability strap. The nose is clamped rigid; only the tail droops. The rolled tail sits above the tyre, so the roll axis must stay short - this is exactly why the min-height rule matters here.

render.basis: Height is a single published figure and is already the packed height, confirmed against assets/products/apidura/expedition-saddle-pack-9l-2.jpg, where the 16 cm body depth measures right against the saddle rails. products.name: Handlebar Pack
products.dims_raw: MIN 30 cm / MAX 54 cm width; 15 cm height; bar clearance MIN 4.5 / MAX 6.9 cm; 3 cm stem drop
products.dims_note: The local "photo" for this product is an SVG dimension diagram with the numerals converted to outlines; I rendered it in headless Chrome and read it directly. It gives 15 cm height, MIN 30 / MAX 54 cm width, bar clearance MIN 4.5 - 6.9 cm and a 3 cm stem drop. len takes the MAX (unfurled) width per the rule. Height is a single figure. NO fore-aft depth is published anywhere: wid is inferred equal to the height because the section is round - that axis is unverified, hence confidence medium.

geometry.notes: Structured centre section with a rounded-rectangular section, not a limp burrito. The diagram shows a squared-off body between the two BarSpace mounts with the roll-down cones extending symmetrically out to each side; a notch is cut into the bottom-centre to clear the steerer/head tube. The dashed outline on the diagram shows the fully-unrolled envelope reaching 54 cm.

closure.hardware: roll-down at both ends, each closed with a g-hook

details.reflective: two reflective slots each side of the front face (visible on the diagram)
details.accessoryMounts: two integrated 3-prong mounts for a light or GPS, plus Anchor Rails
details.fabric: laminated waterproof ripstop, matte charcoal-black, RF-welded seams, Hypalon reinforcement patches, yellow EXPEDITION tag and yellow accent stitching

mount.notes: Does NOT touch the bar. Two rigid BarSpace modules clamp the bar and hold the pack off it. CORRECTION (read directly off the plan view on assets/products/apidura/full/expedition-handlebar-pack/dimensions-1.png): the 3 cm is the FORE-AFT standoff, from the front of the bar tube to the pack's rear face. The MIN 4.5 / MAX 6.9 cm is the adjustable SPACING BETWEEN THE TWO MODULES, measured between their inner and outer edges respectively, so they can straddle stems of different widths - it is not a clearance from the bar, which is how this note previously read. No vertical drop is published; the on-bike photographs put the pack's top edge about a centimetre under the bar tube, with the whole 15/17 cm of height below it. A preload strap cinches the steerer and a stability cord runs round bar and stem. The 9L is specced for bars 42 cm and narrower, the 14L for 44 cm and wider.

module.basis: reach_mm is the same 3 cm already in mount.clearance.bar_mm - fore-aft, from the front of the bar TUBE to the pack's rear face, off the plan view on dimensions-1.png. spacing_mm is the adjustable distance between the two modules (published MIN 4.5 / MAX 6.9 cm) so they can straddle a stem. rise_mm is the vertical gap the module holds between the bar tube and the pack's top face, scaled off on-bike-1.jpg; it is not published. Round 4 held all three in the builder as BARSPACE_SPACING / BARSPACE_RISE and gave them to every pack whose attachment string matched /barspace/i; the builder now uses generic bracket-class defaults and detects a bracket by the class of hardware, not the trade name.

render.basis: Read off the maker dimension diagram, which I rendered from the outlined-numeral SVG (assets/products/apidura/expedition-handlebar-pack-9l-1.jpg) - it is a front elevation of the pack as mounted, so 15 cm is the drawn height. The roll shortens the WIDTH: MIN 30 cm against the MAX 54 cm in dims_cm.len.

products.name: Frame Pack
products.dims_raw: 38.5 cm top length; 26 cm bottom length; 10 cm and 12 cm heights; 2.5 cm rear height; Tapered Width: 6.5 - 6 cm (2.56 - 2.36 in)
products.dims_note: Zippered pack with no roll range, so no MIN/MAX to resolve. len is the top-tube edge; hgt is the deepest of the published heights; wid is the wide end of the 6.5 -> 6 cm taper. The much shorter published bottom length is the taper at both ends and is carried in geometry.taper.

geometry.notes: Rounded triangle, NOT a wedge and NOT deepest at the head tube. Straight top edge on the top tube; small vertical end faces at BOTH ends; the bottom runs shallowly deeper from the seat-tube end, reaches its deepest belly at the published "bottom length" (26 of 38.5 cm, 30 of 43, 31 of 46, 36 of 49 - 68 to 74% of the length) and then blades straight up ALONG THE DOWN TUBE to a small head-tube tip. dimensions-4.png for the 5.7 L reads 15 cm at the seat-tube end, 18 cm at the belly and 7.5 cm at the head-tube face. The seat-tube end is the DEEP one; the head-tube end is the tip. A notch is cut out of the bottom-front to clear downtube bottle bosses. Taper convention for this slot: nose = the HEAD-TUBE end face divided by hgt, tail = the SEAT-TUBE end face divided by hgt. Apidura's own spec line calls the seat-tube end "front" and the head-tube end "rear", which is the reverse of the bike, and an earlier pass copied those labels straight into nose/tail - so every bag in this slot was drawn back to front. Corrected 10 Aug against the maker dimension drawings.

products.dims_note: THE WEAKEST RECORD IN THIS FILE - read before using. Width and depth are confirmed in the page text (depth 30 cm is quoted verbatim). The HEIGHT is not: the page publishes it only inside an outlined-numeral SVG diagram, and the fetched text returns nothing for it. The stored value was 24.5 cm, which an earlier pass reached by back-computing the height that yields the rated litres over the footprint - exactly the fabrication this spec forbids. I have set hgt to 10 cm, the MIN of the 10 - 40 cm range reported from the diagram, which is what the rule demands, but I could not independently verify that 10/40 pair, so verified is false. A builder wanting the bag to look packed should use roughly 25 - 30 cm; 10 cm is the fully collapsed state and will render as a pizza box.

geometry.notes: Two distinct storeys: a rigid squared lower collar built round an HDPE thermoplastic frame and holding its shape absolutely, and a soft roll-top upper that collapses onto it. CORRECTION 10 Aug: this note and render.basis both put the collar at 'about a third' of the packed height. Measured off on-bike-5.jpg against the known 41 cm width it is 0.55 - and 0.55 is also what the published dimensions say, because MIN 10 cm is the height with the roll taken all the way down, i.e. the collar and nothing else, against a packed height of 18 cm. The collar walls SPLAY: dimensions-1/-3 draw the rim overhanging the base by a few percent all the way round, and the soft upper rises from inside that rim. The roll lies ACROSS the bike and is rolled toward the REAR - the two fold spirals show at the far left and right of the straight-on front view in on-bike-5. Over it, hinged behind the roll, is a webbing-edged MESH panel that folds forward over the roll and clips down onto the front collar (feature-4 shows tent poles stuffed under it); it is narrower than the roll, so the spirals stay visible outboard of its edges. The front face of the collar is the graphic face - white bee logo centred, two big yellow chevron blocks, two reflective slots, two side-release buckles.

closure.hardware: magnetic seal in the roll, then a compression panel that folds over the top and down the front onto a G-hook

straps.note: CORRECTION 10 Aug: was 3. dimensions-1 and dimensions-3 are front elevations of this bag and draw exactly TWO webbing runs dropping off the bottom edge, each with a side-release buckle on the front face, and the spacing they dimension (7.5 cm on the 20L, 12 cm on the 30L) is between those two. on-bike-5.jpg shows the same two straps continuing down past the collar to the rack. The side hardware the old count was probably folding in is the G-hook pair that closes the ROLL, which is the 'compression / top / g_hook' entry below, not a rack attachment.

details.structure: reinforced HDPE thermoplastic frame in the lower collar, silicone grips moulded into the base
details.reflective: two reflective slots either side of the logo on the front collar
details.fabric: laminated waterproof ripstop, matte charcoal-black, RF-welded seams, Hypalon reinforcement patches, yellow EXPEDITION tag and yellow accent stitching

mount.notes: RACK ONLY. TWO webbing straps pass under a front rack platform and buckle on the FRONT face (corrected 10 Aug from 'three ... on the sides' — see the note on straps[0]); the silicone-gripped base sits flat on the rails. There is no bar mount at all, so on a 56 cm drop-bar gravel bike with no front rack this cannot be fitted. Base strap spacing is 12 cm, which is what a rack platform has to match.

render.basis: Minimum of the reported 10 - 40 cm range, as the rule requires. FLAGGING A CONFLICT: 10 cm is not a plausible drawn height for a 30L rack pack and will render as a pizza box. Measuring the mounted bag in assets/products/apidura/expedition-front-rack-pack-30l-1.jpg against its known 41 cm width puts the packed height at roughly 15 - 20 cm, of which the rigid lower collar is 0.55 (corrected 10 Aug from 'about a third'; the published MIN 10 cm IS that collar, because it is the height with the roll taken all the way down, and 10 / 18 = 0.55). A builder wanting the bag to look loaded should use ~18 cm. I have left hgt_cm at the rule-mandated minimum rather than deviate silently; note also that the 10/40 pair itself is unverified (see dims_note).
render.conflict: 10cm is the published minimum of Apidura's 10-40cm range, but renders a 30L rack pack as a slab. 18cm measured off the on-bike photo against the known published width; the reviewer recommended this figure in `basis` and it is now applied rather than left as prose.
